column2: req_desc

Desk access journey
A new desk signs up, signs in and out, changes its password so that the person's other sessions end, and creates, reads, renames and deletes a customer, with the status codes published in API.

Desks kept apart
One desk naming another desk's customer, hire, file, invoice or run by its identifier, in an address or inside a request body, gets the not-found answer and nothing from it, however many requests from two desks interleave.

Public site journey
The visitor reads the home, occasion, Fleet and Terms pages, while the slim bar, search overlay, Menu panel, question accordions, section rises, client marks, Message us ring and `On this page` rail follow Interactions and `Get a free quote` from an occasion page opens the form with that occasion chosen, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Public pages in the first response
Every public page answers from the server with its text in the first response, visible with no script, in print and under reduced motion.

Bounded public search
Search runs on the server over the public pages only, and over-long search text or over-deep JSON is refused within a second as API publishes.

Journey ticket journey
The customer walks three steps with one address each, with Back, Forward and reload keeping everything typed, each value travelling as one element into its ticket line and carrying on from where it is when changed in flight, the ticket moving from side panel to bottom bar and sheet at exactly 1024 px, and journey types keeping what was typed, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Pick-up clock rules
Today and Tomorrow, the hour list, short notice, the missing hour, the repeated hour and the return-after-pick-up rule follow the server's UK clock as Business rules publishes, whatever the device clock says.

Request limit, trap field and stored as sent
The sixth request in the window for one folded email is refused with a UK time, a filled `website` field stores nothing behind a normal thanks, and an accepted request is kept byte for byte as sent.

Address lookup journey
From, To and each stop use one combobox that asks once after the typing pauses, reuses what the page already has, ignores older replies, follows the combobox pattern, closes only the list on Escape and carries on when the provider fails, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Address provider rules
Address lookups go through the app's server to the published provider paths with at most a 5-second wait, a typed address is stored unchecked and marked on the desk, and postcodes print in the published form.

Enquiries journey
Filters, search and paging live in the address, an older search reply never shows, a refused state change goes back with its copy and focus kept, and Back returns to the same filters and scroll with focus on the row opened, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Stable list and merging
The enquiry list keeps 25 per page in the published stable order so a row added while reading neither repeats nor skips one, and requests sharing a folded email or telephone merge under the earlier reference.

Trip plan journey
Stops reorder by drag, touch and `Move up` and `Move down` with focus kept, one provider call per reorder and older replies ignored, a failed route keeps the last good one, and a typed plan is kept or refused in the published order, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Fewest vehicles plan
The suggested plan and the miles follow the published ordering and worked examples exactly, and a larger plan is kept and marked.

Operators journey
The arranger refreshes the directory, uploads and reads back papers, sees each operator's standing for a hire and meets the file-store outage copy with nothing half-written, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Directory all or nothing
`Refresh directory` reads every provider page, one failing page leaves the list exactly as it was, and an operator the directory no longer names stays marked.

Operator papers kept exactly
Papers are judged by their first bytes and never their name or stated type, kept byte for byte in MinIO, and limited by the published file-part size answered before authentication.

Clear for the hire's last day
An operator is `Clear` only if every required paper covers the hire's last day, with the school DBS date at exactly three years, and one expiry mail goes per paper as Business rules publishes.

Operator bids journey
The arranger asks chosen operators, each operator prices, changes or withdraws by private address, the table's sort stays in the address and scrolls in its own named frame at 375, an operator not `Clear` cannot be awarded and losers get one closing mail each, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Bid page shows one hire
The private bid page and every response behind it show only that hire's route, dates, vehicles and party size, work by address alone, accept only the published prices and refuse every misformed price.

Bid window edge
The server alone decides the bid window at each read and press, so a press in the second of `closesAt` is accepted, a press in any later second gets the published refusal and the page has ended from then on.

One award wins
Of two awards at once exactly one wins and the other reads the published line, and pressing `Award` twice sends no extra mail.

Quote building journey
Totals change in place on every input with one announcement and no older reply winning, and the arranger sends the quote from a screen that keeps what was typed, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Exact quote money
Selling price, VAT per vehicle and deposit at and over each limit match the worked examples to the penny on screen and in the API.

Rate tables by date
A rate table takes effect on its chosen date, so an edit changes the future only, a sent quote keeps its sending day's rates and two tables with one date are refused.

Stale quote edit
Saving over a newer quote is refused with the published line and what was typed stays on screen.

Customer page journey
The customer uses the page by touch at 375x812 in English, Polish or Urdu with `lang` and `dir` from the server before any script, the language held in the address, a typed-name acceptance refused as typed and `I've sent the deposit` changing no money, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Quote end decided at the server
A quote ends at the end of the fifth UK calendar day after sending, across a clock change, decided at each read and press with no sweep and never by the device clock.

Customer copies stay private
Bought-in prices, margin, operator names and unsigned notes reach no customer page, response field, mail or PDF, and an acceptance request can change only what is published.

Published customer strings
The customer page and run sheet print the published table of strings, date forms, money form and Polish and Urdu counts character for character, and a replaced page, an ended page and an unknown address each answer as published.

Payments journey
The arranger brings a statement in through a preview, sees matched, unmatched, money-out, already-seen and refused rows, presses `Bring in` and sees money per vehicle and `Money held` change, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Statement reading
Statement encoding, dates, quoted amounts, the reference grammar and the already-seen rule follow Business rules, and bringing the same file twice changes nothing.

Allocation and paired ledger
Money goes to vehicles by departure then list order to the penny as worked, every movement writes two ledger lines, each booking's lines sum to zero and `Money held` always equals the ledger.

Balance reminder
One reminder mail goes at the first daily check from 10 days before departure in UK dates while a balance is owed, as qualified in Business rules.

Safe downloads
Passenger and payment files neutralise risky cell starts with a straight apostrophe, are in UTF-8 with a byte order mark and carry Polish file names correctly.

Diary journey
The week lives in the address with one roving Tab stop, Alt with an arrow moves a hire and keeps focus through the refresh, drag works by pointer and touch with Escape putting it back, a driver clash is refused and the grid becomes an agenda at 375, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Wall time kept
A hire moved across a clock change keeps its local wall time with the published instants, and a week holding a change shows its 23 or 25 hour day.

Duty ribbon journey
One CSS pixel stands for one real minute, the break moves by drag, touch and arrows, blocks reflow once and carry on when interrupted, the breach shows from its exact minute without relying on colour, the table says the same as the ribbon and a breached run cannot be confirmed, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Hours limits in real minutes
Each published limit is judged in real elapsed minutes across clock changes and read at `GET /api/runs/<id>/hours`, and `Add second driver` clears them.

Passenger list and seat plan journey
The arranger brings in or types names, swaps people by keys, pointer and touch with focus on the seat dropped on and the published announcement, and prints the plan, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Seat grid and per-head split
Every size's grid adds up as published, wheelchair users take only the seats by the lift, adults short shows its published count, and a per-head split sums to the vehicle's total with earlier names taking the extra pennies.

Driver run sheet journey
The driver follows one private run sheet at 375x812 and 812x375 in English or Polish with big presses at each stop, and the arranger accepts charges once, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Driver told only when accepted
`Driver told` appears only after ntfy has accepted the message, one message per press on the published topic, and with ntfy down nothing is marked as told.

Queued presses counted once
With no signal the page and its queue survive a reload, presses are sent in order with their own repeat key and `secondsAgo`, and a replay returns the first answer and counts nothing twice.

Waiting charges
Waiting, the airport rule from the flight provider and comfort stops follow the worked amounts, and charges reach the booking only after `Accept charges`, once, by paired ledger lines.

Changes and cancellations journey
A change shows old and new side by side, a moved price gives a fresh private page while the old address has ended, refunds and amounts owed show per vehicle, and `Cancel booking` pressed twice records one, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Cancellation charges
Days are counted between UK calendar dates from the typed notice, each band gives its worked amount with the deposit floor and total cap, and a departure already gone cannot be cancelled.

Documents journey
The strip follows the server with each step's check drawn once and never again on a refresh, an issued invoice lists its history in order, and the PDF holds Polish letters and no margin or bought-in price, and its screen meets the screen rules.

PDFs kept only when confirmed
A document reads `Stored` only after Gotenberg has answered and MinIO has confirmed, and either outage saves nothing, shows its copy and takes no number.

Gapless numbers per desk
Invoice and credit note numbers run with no gaps per desk by UK calendar year, two issued at the same moment take consecutive numbers, and the sixth download in the window is refused with a UK time.

Aftercare journey
The arranger logs complaints and found items, returns an item only after recording the owner's details, closes and brings back a customer and brings in an old sheet, and its screen meets the screen rules.

Complaint and holding dates
Complaint reply dates count working days in England and Wales with the holiday provider's good, failing, last-good and none states, and holding dates and `Past holding date` follow the worked month ends at each read.

Close, bring back, erase
A closed customer comes back exactly as it was during the wait, then is erased with its MinIO objects gone, private pages ended, invoices marked `Erased customer` and ledger sums intact, and with MinIO down it stays `Erasing`.

Old customer sheet
Sheet rows match by folded email or telephone, a no-match row adds, a one-match row fills only empty fields, a two-match row goes to the review list and changes nothing, and a re-import creates nothing.

Cross-cutting journey
The route sweep holds on every signed-in route and private page, sign-in takes focus on its heading and lands on `/enquiries`, and returning after an ended session keeps the address and the draft.

One error shape and ladder
Every error uses the one published body with no stack trace, SQL, path or library name, one ladder decides every multi-fault request, and only published endpoints and pages exist.

Exact starting state
The first sign-in shows exactly the customers, operators, enquiries, bookings, runs, seat plan, ledger and invoice that Seed data prints.

Motion system
Every motion in the app runs on the browser's animation timeline at exactly one of the three published durations, nothing loops forever, and reduced motion gives the same end states at once.

Bands and counter-top look
Public and desk screens carry the card's full-bleed plum and cyan bands, square shapes, type and named seed components as Visual design describes, with the floor-to-ceiling cyan form as the working centrepiece.

Real services behind the screens
The source reads every credential from the environment and stores files, mail, PDFs and pushes through the real providers, with each stated rule decided on the server.
`/app/run.json` holds string `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and is the only way the app is installed, built and served.
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` names every shipped package and font with its licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`).

Shipped packages (the production dependency tree, `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) carry only MIT, MIT-0, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or CC0-1.0 licences, and a font or font package only OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are Postgres and MinIO; no Valkey, SQLite, file-based database or other store is added on the server.
Fonts, icons and drawings are self-hosted or generated by the project; no page loads anything from another origin.
No image, icon, text or code is taken from any reference site; all imagery is generated SVG or uploaded by users.
Credentials are read from the environment; none is committed, and the compose or service configuration provided is left untouched.
